text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's Austrian newspapers.

- The ruling Social Democrats suffered their worst ever defeat, while the far-right Freedom Party scored a historic triumph in Sunday's European Parliamentary elections. The conservative junior coalition partner People's Party led the EU polls, but trailed in third place in Vienna state elections held on the same day. The socialists lost their absolute control of the capital of nearly 50 years. Greens and Liberals scored below the ten percent in both elections.

- The division of the 110 billion schilling debt of state-owned Post & Telekom Austria Beteilgung (PTB) and its unit Post & Telekom Austria has led to a dispute between the two. The latter refuses to take on the agreed 66 billion schilling part of the debt, after Finance Minister Viktor Klima handed over the post's bank P.S.K. to the PTB to be privatised.

- Energy provider Verbund will rationalise some 300 million schillings more than the planned one billion by the year 2003. Verbund plans to bid for Austria's third mobile phone network licence with Austrian railways and United Telekom Austria, a group of provincial energy providers.
- The introduction of a single currency in the European Union will raise interest rates, while money will be made from uncertainty, Investkredit expects.
- German tyre maker Continental welcomes a vote by workers at Austrian unit Semperit, in which 80 percent decided not to strike against proposed production cuts.

- Trade with emerging markets is slowing down as the growth potential appears to be fading, economic research institute IHS says. However trade deficits in these countries are seen as a danger with imports growing faster than exports.
- Gerhard Randa, chief of Bank Austria, says he expects the government's 17 percent stake in the bank will be privatised soon.
- Savings bank Die Erste is still interested in a holding for Creditanstalt and Die Erste.
- The Interior Ministry refuses to help airport group Flughafen with investments costing 375 million schillings which must made according to the European Union's Schengen agreement.
- Workers unions want structural reforms ahead of plans to liberalise work hours.
- J.P. Morgan's information memorandum on the privatisation of Creditanstalt will be ready by the end of the week. The tender will be based on the outcome of it.
